newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 18.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:

* "Star Wars" by News Corp's 20th Century Fox topped a record-breaking Presidents' Day weekend with a studio-estimated $21.8 million haul. The classic helped the movie-going universe expand to an estimated $125 million for the four-day frame, a huge jump compared with last year's $96 million. Star Wars accumulated $99 million in the first 17 days of its Special Edition re-release, bringing its lifetime total to $421.8 million. "Absolute Power," by Time Warner's Castle Rock and Sony Corp's Columbia opened in second place with $16.8 million.

* "Asteroid," by General Electric NBC, had the highest overnight ratings for any movie this season, with part one posting a 19.5 rating and 28 share from 9-11 p.m. in the 36 metered markets on Sunday, according to Nielsen. For the night, NBC finished with a 14.2/21. National ratings will be released later this week.
* "The English Patient" and "The People vs. Larry Flynt" hogged the limelight at the Berlin Film Festival over the weekend, with both pictures already appearing set to win awards.
* Kirstie Alley will star in Walt Disney Telefilms' "Toothless."

* Last week Disney-owned Miramax Films and Viacom's Paramount Pictures were in final negotiations on a deal to co-acquire and co-distribute the Gwyneth Paltrow movie "Sliding Doors" from Sydney Pollack's Mirage Entertainment. If the deal goes through, the picture, financed by Guy East and Nigel Sinclair's Intermedia, will be distributed theatrically in the U.S. by Miramax and in other English-language territories by Paramount. Intermedia has the film for the rest of the world.
